cases.description:
Launch an autonomous agent for complex, multi-step tasks. Agent types:
- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. (Tools: *)
- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. (Tools: read, bash, grep, find, ls)
- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. (Tools: read, bash, grep, find, ls)

Custom agents: .pi/agents/<name>.md (project) or <agentDir>/agents/<name>.md (global).

Notes:
- description: 3-5 words (shown in UI). Prompts must be self-contained — the agent has not seen this conversation.
- Parallel work: one message, multiple Agent calls — they run concurrently.
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass run_in_background: false only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — if the user asks before the notification arrives, say it's still running.
- The result is not shown to the user — summarize it for them. Verify an agent's claimed code changes before reporting work done.
- resume continues a previous agent by ID; steer_subagent messages a running one.
- isolation: "worktree" gives the agent its own git worktree (removed on completion); changes land on a branch named in the result.

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform.

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task (shown in UI).

name.description: Optional memorable name for this agent, e.g. "auth-audit", so it can be addressed as `@name` at the prompt and by steer_subagent / get_subagent_result. Letters, digits, `_` and `-`. Worth setting when several agents of the same type run at once; omit for one-off work. The agent stays reachable by its type either way.

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use. Available types: general-purpose, Explore, Plan. Custom agents from .pi/agents/*.md (project) or <agentDir>/agents/*.md (global) are also available.

model.description: Model for this delegated task. Choose based on the task's complexity, required capabilities, and cost/latency trade-offs — not merely the parent's model. Accepts "provider/modelId" or a fuzzy name. If omitted, inherits the configured agent model or the parent's model. Agent-file model pins take precedence.

thinking.description: Thinking level: off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max. Reasoning effort for this delegated task. Choose independently of the parent's effort: lower for bounded mechanical work, higher for difficult analysis or verification. If omitted, inherits the agent's configured effort or the parent's. Agent-file thinking pins take precedence.

max_turns.description: Maximum number of agentic turns per run, including each resume. Frontmatter takes precedence; 0 means unlimited. Omit to inherit the configured or stored budget.

run_in_background.description: Defaults to true — the agent runs detached, returning its ID immediately, and you are notified on completion. Set false only when your very next action depends on the result; the call then blocks and returns the agent's full output inline.

resume.description: Optional agent ID to resume from. Continues from previous context. Resumes detached like any other spawn; pass run_in_background: false to block and get the result inline. Each resume gets a fresh max_turns budget, governed by the existing agent's type, not subagent_type. An agent can only be resumed once its current run has finished — use steer_subagent to reach one mid-run.

isolated.description: If true, agent gets no extension/MCP tools — only built-in tools.

inherit_context.description: If true, fork parent conversation into the agent. Default: false (fresh context).

isolation.description: Isolation mode. Default "off". "off" runs the agent in the current checkout, the same as omitting the field. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo (a copy cannot see uncommitted or staged changes in the main checkout).

schedule.description: Opt-in only — fire later instead of now. Omit to run immediately (the default, almost always correct). Formats: 6-field cron ("0 0 9 * * 1" = 9am Mon), interval ("5m"/"1h"), one-shot ("+10m" or ISO). Forces run_in_background; incompatible with inherit_context and resume. Returns job ID.

script.description: Inline workflow source. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description }`.

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file, absolute or relative to the project. Takes precedence over `script` — this is how you re-run an edited workflow.

name.description: Name of a saved workflow — `<name>.js` in .pi/workflows/, .agents/workflows/ or the user's agent dir. Lowest precedence: `scriptPath` and `script` both win over it.

args.description: Exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Must be JSON-shaped.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run id of an earlier workflow in this session. Its unchanged leading agent() calls return their recorded results instantly; the first changed or failed call, and everything after it, runs live. Same script and args means nothing re-runs.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.
